serious_errors.materiality: Reading historic acceptance as a basis for section 115 estoppel against a fresh 1941 forfeiture would materially affect possession rights, yet representation and reliance are not shown. The report merely invokes the possibility, so seriousness is unresolved.

important_omissions: The High Court allowed the plaintiff’s cross-objections regarding trees and costs while dismissing defendant No. 1’s second appeal; the report gives only the dismissal, obscuring the separate procedural outcome (S721f1d767bf4).

The 1938 court rejected the specific defences that rent was not fixed for the disputed property and that the plaintiff had to seek payment, which bears on the repeated defence advanced in 1941 (Se97eddf17deb).

The 1938 District Judge, on the plaintiff’s appeal from relief against forfeiture, refused to upset the grant while warning against a later fourth grant; this different historical appellate posture is not distinguished (Sf043641ff118).

Possession of the suit lands actually passed to the plaintiff in April and September 1943, while defendant No. 1 retained the two structures on survey No. 86/2; the report mentions the conditional decree but not its execution and the possession split (Sc53fc5712708).

The saved pre-Act rights and liabilities under Transfer of Property Act section 2(c) are not expressly applied to the 1863 lease; this could affect whether the section 111(g) notice rule governs (L61826e66207e).

The report does not confront whether the express contractual default provisions meet the section 111(g)(1) requirement for a lessor’s right to re-enter, as distinct from merely saying tenant rights end (L5d1f299e4f9f; S3417d2a4167c; S80566af1f5f0).

The section 114 relief conditions of paying or tendering arrears, interest and full suit costs, or furnishing sufficient security, are not matched against the evidence; a pleaded offer of rent is not automatically a proven statutory tender (L76b2d960cce4; Saa2df4bbd6db).
Section 112’s knowledge requirement and proviso concerning rent accepted after an ejectment suit are not addressed when invoking earlier waivers; no present-1941 waiver is shown (L625a28da96a6).

The possibility of the agricultural-lease exclusion in section 117 and the need for a relevant State notification are not tested; the CASE materials identify inam lands but do not conclusively establish the threshold agricultural purpose or notification (Ld4e6570d01b0; S7d318e964c98).
reports.main_answer_reason: The report substantively reconstructs the lease, parcel distinction, opposing positions, appellate rationales and both unresolved questions, but omits the 1938 defences and plaintiff appeal, section 2(c) saving, section 114 conditions, and incorrectly identifies section 112 as an Evidence Act provision. Its characterization of 1931 acceptance as waiver also exceeds the explicit source statement.
uncertainties: The withheld Supreme Court reasoning and disposition cannot be reconstructed from the lower-court holdings; neither the ultimate need for notice nor final relief is certified.

The abbreviated High Court excerpts state the equity/good-conscience reasoning on notice but do not fully establish whether its distinct statutory grounds exactly matched the District Judge’s pre-Act rationale.
The rent-note terms and competing demand/tender claims are described through judgment excerpts rather than underlying instruments or testimony; the allegations are not independent findings.
The money-order acceptance in 1931 alone does not settle whether a forfeiture had occurred, was known to the lessor, or was waived.
The legal effect, if any, of the 1928 and 1934 historical waivers on the fresh 1941 default is not established by the supplied materials.
The applicable statutory version, geographic extension and agricultural-lease treatment cannot be assumed solely because particular LAW excerpts were supplied.
The record does not establish a distinct intentional representation, induced belief, and reliance supporting Evidence Act section 115 estoppel for the present suit.
The record does not resolve whether the tenant made a legally sufficient tender of arrears, interest and costs or supplied security for section 114 relief.
